findings.text: `int(nth)` silently wraps for values outside int range. With N=uint64 and nth=math.MaxUint64, n becomes -1 and the last element is returned instead of an out-of-bounds error. On 32-bit builds, int64(1<<32) becomes 0 and returns the first element.

raw:
Conversion int(nth) can truncate: for uint64 or int64 large values wrapping (on 64-bit, uint64 > MaxInt64 becomes negative, so e.g. 2^64-1 → -1 returns last element instead of error). Also int64 on 32-bit truncation.
